articles.title: AI First
articles.rule: Use AI to analyse, explain and recommend while preserving human control.

articles.title: Configuration over Hardcoding
articles.rule: Business rules must originate from configuration or explicit contracts.

articles.title: Behaviour before Components
articles.rule: Validate complete behaviour chains, including forbidden outcomes.

articles.title: Human Approval for Risk
articles.rule: High-impact actions require explicit human approval.

articles.title: Explainability Required
articles.rule: Every automated verdict must include reason and evidence.

articles.title: Registered Capabilities
articles.rule: Every platform capability must be registered with owner and dependencies.

articles.title: Contracted Behaviour
articles.rule: Every user-visible capability must have a behaviour contract.

articles.title: Release Integrity
articles.rule: Every release must prove feature, impact and platform consistency.

articles.title: Controlled Complexity
articles.rule: Complexity increases require justification and registered technical debt.

articles.title: No Vendor Lock-in
articles.rule: Features request capabilities and must not depend directly on a specific AI provider.

articles.title: Shared Experience Context
articles.rule: Channels and touchpoints share one governed experience context rather than isolated silos.

articles.title: Industry-neutral Core
articles.rule: Platform Core must remain independent of any specific industry, tenant, customer or experience.

articles.title: Domain Isolation
articles.rule: Industry-specific logic belongs in domain packs above Platform Core.

articles.title: Contract-first Data
articles.rule: Important platform data must use versioned, traceable, privacy-aware and transport-neutral canonical contracts.

articles.title: Shared Context by Contract
articles.rule: Cross-channel context must be purpose-bound, minimal, expiring and contract-based. Persistent identity or personal data requires explicit policy and approval.

articles.title: Evidence before approval
articles.principle: A release may only be approved when the promised behaviour has observable evidence at every required test level. Missing evidence is not a pass.
articles.enforcement: Verification Governance derives mandatory test suites from capability profiles and blocks incomplete evidence.

articles.title: Human-Governed AI
articles.rule: AI may observe, analyse, recommend, implement and verify only within explicit risk policies; strategic, high-impact or irreversible actions require human approval.

articles.title: Continuous Measured Improvement
articles.rule: Improvements must progress from evidence through verification and measurement before the platform records learning or claims impact.

articles.title: Governed Actions
articles.rule: Every platform action must use the canonical action contract, carry evidence and verification, and obey risk-based human approval before execution.

articles.title: Evidence before interpretation
articles.principle: AI may interpret observations, but it may not be treated as the primary source of facts. User-facing conclusions must be traceable to verified evidence and their confidence may not exceed evidence quality.

articles.title: AI Decision UX
articles.rule: Every user-facing AI recommendation must present one clear primary CTA, explicit alternative outcomes, and an understandable consequence for approval, editing, postponement and rejection.

articles.title: Closed Loop UX
articles.rule: Every approved AI action must update platform state visibly in the same workflow, remove the completed task, calculate the next best action, and surface any pending publication work.

articles.title: AI Output Quality
articles.rule: AI-genereret brugerindhold må kun vises, når det har bestået formålsspecifik semantisk kvalitetsvalidering. Uverificeret output sendes til manuel kontrol frem for at blive præsenteret som publiceringsklart.

articles.title: Domain Context before Generation
articles.rule: AI must resolve verified domain context before generating domain-specific content. Unknown facts must be confidence-qualified or sent for clarification.

articles.title: Adaptive Clarification Loop
articles.principle: AI must ask only relevant questions, present clear answer paths and use negative answers to request the missing corrective context.
rules: One targeted question at a time
No answer path may end without a visible state update
A negative answer must trigger a relevant follow-up when a factual gap remains
Unknown and deferred answers must not be treated as verified facts
Human answers become versioned verified domain facts

articles.title: Continuous Domain Discovery
articles.principle: Domain Intelligence must continuously derive relevant uncertainties from current tasks and verified knowledge. A zero-question state is valid only when sufficient context is documented for the active work.

articles.title: Typed Relationships before Inference
articles.rule: Domain relationships must be typed, reference valid objects and carry an explicit evidence status before AI may use them for interpretation or generation. Derived relationships require confidence and must never be presented as human-verified facts.

articles.title: Explainable Impact before Action
articles.rule: Verified domain changes must be analysed against typed relationships before actions are proposed. Every proposed action must identify affected objects, supporting evidence, risk and required human approval. No content may be published automatically from an impact analysis.

articles.title: Every Recommendation Must Be Actionable
articles.rule: Every user-facing recommendation must provide an executable path, explicit defer and reject outcomes, context transfer to a valid target workspace, completion evidence and closed-loop state updates.

articles.title: Plain-Language Actions
articles.rule: User-facing actions must explain the outcome in ordinary language, hide internal architecture terms by default, present one clear primary action, and offer a guided multi-action flow when several improvements are available.

articles.title: One Click to Work
articles.rule: A recommendation must open the concrete work item with context already selected, without forcing the user to search inside a general workspace.

articles.title: Automatic Completion
articles.rule: A guided flow must close automatically when all tasks are complete, present a concise result and offer the next relevant step without requiring a redundant stop or close action.

articles.title: Primary CTA Runtime Verification
articles.rule: A primary user action is not verified until the executable interaction chain proves that it changes the visible state or reaches a clear error terminal state. Silent or stale actions block release.
